entities.name: ATP synthase epsilon chain
observations: 133 aa bacterial protein; exact sequence match to reviewed UniProt entry A4ITI8 from Geobacillus thermodenitrificans.
Predicted molecular weight is 14.48 kDa and theoretical pI is 9.43.
Contains ATP-synt_DE_N (PF02823) at residues 3–85 and ATP-synt_DE (PF00401) at residues 86–131.
Reference annotations place it as a peripheral component of the plasma-membrane F-type ATP synthase complex.

The epsilon chain is a non-catalytic structural/regulatory subunit associated with the F1 catalytic sector; the retrieved database annotation assigns ATP synthase complex and rotational proton-transport activity at the complex level, not independent catalysis by epsilon.

source_tools.relevance: Exact sequence match and sequence-derived properties

entities.name: F-type ATP synthase complex
observations: F-type ATP synthase couples proton-gradient-driven rotation through F0 to ATP synthesis in the F1 catalytic sector.
The epsilon chain is one copy in the F1 sector together with alpha, beta, gamma, and delta subunits.

entities.name: Epsilon subunit functional assignment
observations: Sequence identity of 100% over the full length to reviewed A4ITI8 provides high-confidence identification as an ATP synthase epsilon chain.
The protein is predicted to be a small, basic, soluble/peripheral-membrane-associated component rather than a transmembrane proton-channel subunit or standalone enzyme.
